mission: Deliver and integrate DHA into neuronal membranes so the brain maintains a flexible, signal-ready lipid foundation.

stage2a.operation: Owns DHA incorporation, not choline methyl-donor limitation or downstream clinical effects; those associated donor claims remain unresolved for this run.

existing_findings.proposition: DHA is a structural polyunsaturated fatty acid of neuronal membranes; that structural role is not a human dosing or ADHD-treatment rule.

existing_source_assessments.label: McNamara and Carlson (2006)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Long-chain omega-3 fats, especially DHA, are structural components of neuronal membranes relevant to brain development and function.

assessment.study: Narrative review of omega-3 roles in brain development, function and psychopathology risk.
assessment.population: Mixed developmental, animal and human literature summarised in the review.
assessment.result: Identified DHA as a principal membrane PUFA with signalling-architecture implications.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary dose-response or ADHD treatment estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes the structural membrane role of DHA.
assessment.limitations: Review synthesis; not a human incorporation trial.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: LPC-DHA is transported by MFSD2A more efficiently than free or triglyceride-bound DHA; carrier form is a transport property, not a choline-intake or ADHD-dosing rule.

existing_source_assessments.label: Patrick (2019)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Phosphatidylcholine-DHA can generate LPC-DHA, which crosses the blood–brain barrier via MFSD2A more efficiently than non-phospholipid forms.

assessment.study: Review of phosphatidylcholine-DHA transport and APOE4-associated Alzheimer context.
assessment.population: Mixed human genetic and mechanistic literature; not a dietary ADHD sample.
assessment.result: Identified LPC-DHA / MFSD2A as the efficient barrier-transport route.
assessment.limitations: Review; does not show choline intake constrains DHA incorporation.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Phospholipid-bound dietary DHA produced greater gray-matter DHA accretion than triglyceride-bound DHA in neonatal piglets; that animal contrast is not a human dosing or ADHD-treatment rule.

existing_source_assessments.label: Liu et al. (2014)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Phospholipid-bound dietary DHA produced higher brain gray-matter DHA accretion than triglyceride-bound DHA in neonatal piglets.

assessment.study: Controlled comparison of matched DHA intake as phospholipid versus triglyceride.
assessment.result: Approximately 1.9-fold greater gray-matter DHA accretion from the phospholipid form.
assessment.effect_magnitude: About 1.9-fold accretion contrast in that animal model.
assessment.evidence_summary: Shows delivery form can change brain DHA accretion in piglets.
assessment.limitations: Animal model; not a human dose and not a choline-intake test.

existing_supportive_evidence.label: Colletti et al. (2021)
existing_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews krill-oil phospholipid omega-3 composition and applications.
existing_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Sourcing and clinical-application review; not a neuronal-membrane incorporation measurement.

existing_supportive_evidence.label: Patted et al. (2024)
existing_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Broader omega-3 source and function review, including contaminant-context discussion.
existing_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: General source review; not a finding on MFSD2A transport or membrane accretion.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Observational multi-nutrient supplementation in ADHD-seeking children is translationally adjacent to attention and emotion scores; it cannot isolate membrane DHA incorporation as the cause.

existing_source_assessments.label: Huss et al. (2010)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Combined PUFA, magnesium and zinc was followed by attention and emotional-problem score changes; membrane DHA cannot be isolated.

assessment.population: Children seeking medical advice for ADHD-related symptoms.
assessment.result: SNAP-IV attention/hyperactivity and SDQ emotional-problem scores improved versus baseline.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Within-cohort score changes; no DHA-only contrast.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supplies ADHD-adjacent outcome context with hard attribution limits.
assessment.limitations: Observational; omega-3/6 plus magnesium and zinc; not membrane DHA.

existing_supportive_evidence.label: Pei-Chen Chang (2021)
existing_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews omega-3 fatty acids in ADHD as personalised-medicine context.
existing_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Narrative review; does not measure neuronal-membrane DHA incorporation.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Human PET estimates of circulating DHA incorporation quantify brain replacement under studied conditions; they do not directly measure oral dose requirements.

existing_source_assessments.label: Umhau et al. (2009)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: PET and plasma measurements supported an estimated adult whole-brain DHA incorporation rate of 3.8 ± 1.7 mg/day.

assessment.result: Measured tracer uptake and plasma DHA were used to calculate whole-brain net incorporation.
assessment.effect_magnitude: 3.8 ± 1.7 mg/day; estimated 911-day half-life using a reported 5 g pool.
assessment.evidence_summary: Quantifies adult brain incorporation rather than oral intake.
assessment.limitations: Steady-state kinetic model; pool size assumed from prior literature; no oral supplementation comparison.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Choline tracing supports contribution to the PEMT-derived LPC-DHA route; separate transport experiments establish LPC-DHA as a brain-delivery substrate.

existing_source_assessments.label: Klatt et al. (2019)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Higher choline intake increased methyl-derived d3-LPC-DHA enrichment but not total plasma LPC-DHA.

assessment.study: Post hoc isotope analysis of a controlled 10-week choline feeding trial with supplemental DHA.
assessment.population: Non-pregnant, pregnant and lactating women; not an adult brain-incorporation experiment.
assessment.result: Figures 5–7 distinguish total LPC-DHA from d3 and d9 enrichment; d3 identifies the methyl-derived route.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No main choline effect on total plasma LPC-DHA; increased d3 enrichment. No brain uptake effect estimated.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports choline contribution to the methyl-derived carrier route.
assessment.limitations: Full Results and figure captions inspected. Plasma enrichment does not isolate net carrier production or brain delivery; reproductive context affects interpretation.

existing_source_assessments.label: Nguyen et al. (2014)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: MFSD2A transported LPC-DHA in cell assays; knockout mice had reduced labelled plasma-to-brain LPC uptake.

assessment.study: Cell transport experiments and Mfsd2a knockout mouse uptake studies.
assessment.population: Cells and mice; not choline-fed adult humans.
assessment.result: Cell and brain uptake experiments establish the LPC-DHA transport substrate.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Reduced labelled uptake after transporter loss; no dietary methyl-donor effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports the carrier-to-brain transport link independently of dietary choline responsiveness.
assessment.limitations: Abstract and figure descriptions inspected; full subscription methods/results not obtained. Transporter loss is not donor inadequacy.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Folate-dependent remethylation and hepatic betaine/BHMT remethylation replenish methionine for SAM-dependent PEMT chemistry, which connects to the independently established methyl-derived LPC-DHA carrier route.

existing_source_assessments.label: Chew et al. (2011)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Donor restriction reduced pathway-specific methyl incorporation in female liver.

assessment.study: Eight-week folate restriction versus otherwise matched control diets with labelled choline. Indexed primary methods, results and discussion assessed.
assessment.population: Male and female Mthfr wild-type and heterozygous mice.
assessment.result: Females had lower hepatic d3-PC enrichment and product/precursor enrichment ratio; males lacked that hepatic response.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Hepatic d3-PC enrichment 30% lower (P=0.017); d3-PC:d9-choline ratio P=0.049.
assessment.evidence_summary: Donor restriction reduced pathway-specific methyl incorporation in female liver.
assessment.limitations: Precursor enrichment, turnover and methyl competition affect this measurement; total PEMT flux was not measured.

existing_source_assessments.label: Kharbanda et al. (2007)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Betaine corrected production under an imposed methylation imbalance.

assessment.study: Control/ethanol liquid diets with or without 1% betaine for four weeks. Primary abstract assessed; full assay methods unavailable.
assessment.result: Betaine restored SAM:SAH balance and reported PEMT-mediated PC production under ethanol exposure.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No usable numerical production estimate in the abstract.
assessment.evidence_summary: Betaine corrected production under an imposed methylation imbalance.
assessment.limitations: Supplement rescue does not establish ordinary betaine deficiency; assay details and ethanol context limit attribution.

preserved_phenome_source_records.rationale: Membrane DHA is a structural context for synaptic signalling {{cite:mcnamara_role_2006}}. An observational multi-nutrient study in children seeking help for ADHD-related symptoms cannot isolate membrane DHA from co-supplemented minerals {{cite:huss_supplementation_2010}}. Omega-3 ADHD reviews remain contextual {{cite:pei-chen_chang_personalised_2021}}.

DHA in neuronal phospholipids supports membrane architecture used in synaptic signalling {{cite:mcnamara_role_2006}} {{cite:patrick_role_2019}}. Delivery form can change accretion in an animal model {{cite:liu_higher_2014}}. Those are structural and transport findings, not cognitive-clarity scores after a human DHA change.

Combined omega-3/6 with magnesium and zinc was followed by fewer emotional-problem scores in an observational ADHD-seeking cohort {{cite:huss_supplementation_2010}}. Membrane DHA remains the mechanism boundary; the multi-nutrient design cannot isolate incorporation {{cite:mcnamara_role_2006}}.

stage2b.clarification: DHA, upstream choline and both folate/betaine KC supply records are retained. No LPC-carrier advantage is transferred to all fish, roe or oils; multiple upstream supplies do not become independent effect multipliers.

section_presentations.label: DHA
section_presentations.reader_description: DHA is the omega-3 fat built into neuronal membranes. Phospholipid-bound DHA changes how the fat is carried for barrier transport; it is not a second independent treatment lever.

type_delivery_metadata.permitted_wording: DHA is a Direct dietary provision of the fatty acid being incorporated into neuronal membranes. Phospholipid-bound DHA is a delivery form, not a second independent clinical lever. This is not an ADHD treatment rule.
type_delivery_metadata.evidence_limitation: Diet can provide DHA for membrane incorporation. That does not establish an ADHD treatment effect or a human dosing rule from the porcine phospholipid comparison.

type_delivery_metadata.permitted_wording: Choline participates in phosphatidylcholine chemistry that can carry DHA. That is not a Direct choline requirement for membrane incorporation.
type_delivery_metadata.evidence_limitation: Patrick and Liu show phospholipid-DHA carrier form, not that dietary choline intake limits DHA incorporation into human neuronal membranes.

type_delivery_metadata.permitted_wording: Folate-derived one-carbon units support [BRS2 PM1 — remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation), replenishing methionine for SAM-dependent [BRS2 PM7 — PEMT formation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm3/brs2-fm3-pm7-phosphatidylcholine-formation), upstream of DHA-bearing LPC carrier delivery.
type_delivery_metadata.evidence_limitation: Supported biochemical supply chain, not a demonstrated increase in net adult brain DHA incorporation. Folate/choline compensation, hepatic BHMT, SAM turnover and carrier remodelling vary by context. Mouse folate effects were sex/tissue dependent; betaine rescue used ethanol-exposed rats. The downstream human tracer study administered choline, not folate or betaine. A donor-specific limiting effect and extra-intake benefit remain unresolved.
